A display device including a display panel; a frame at a rear of the display panel, the frame including a bottom and a sidewall extending from the bottom; a substrate on the frame; a plurality of light sources mounted on the substrate; and a reflecting sheet on the substrate. The reflecting sheet includes a first sheet part on the bottom and having a rectangular shape with a first long side, a second long side opposite the first long side, a first short side adjacent to the first long side and the second long side, and a second short side opposite the first short side, the first sheet part comprising a plurality of holes corresponding to the plurality of light sources; a second sheet part extended from the first sheet part toward the side wall of the frame; and a plurality of dots on the second sheet part, wherein the plurality of dots reduces a reflectance of light, and wherein a size of the plurality of dots increases from a corner of the second sheet part in a first direction parallel to the long sides and a second direction parallel to the short sides.

outputs.L2: A display apparatus comprises a display panel and a frame positioned behind the panel. The frame has a base and a sidewall projecting from the base. A substrate is disposed on the frame and supports multiple light emitters, while a reflective sheet is arranged over the substrate. The reflective sheet has a rectangular first portion located on the frame base. This first portion is bounded by opposing first and second longitudinal edges and opposing first and second transverse edges, with the first transverse edge adjoining both longitudinal edges. It also contains multiple openings respectively aligned with the light emitters. A second portion of the reflective sheet extends from the first portion toward the frame sidewall. outputs.L3:
The display device includes a display panel and a rear frame positioned behind the display panel. The rear frame has a bottom portion and a sidewall extending from the bottom portion. A substrate on which a plurality of light sources is arranged is mounted on the rear frame, and a reflecting sheet is disposed over the substrate.

The reflecting sheet includes a rectangular first sheet portion positioned on the bottom portion of the rear frame. The first sheet portion has a plurality of holes corresponding to the respective light sources, thereby allowing light emitted by the light sources to pass through the reflecting sheet. The reflecting sheet further includes a second sheet portion extending from the first sheet portion toward the sidewall of the rear frame.

A plurality of dots configured to reduce light reflectance is formed on the second sheet portion. The dots are arranged such that their size progressively increases from a corner of the second sheet portion in both a direction parallel to the long side of the second sheet portion and a direction parallel to its short side. This variation in dot size helps control the distribution of reflected light near the sidewall and corner regions of the display device.
outputs.L4:
A display device includes a display panel, a rear frame disposed behind the display panel, and a substrate supported by the rear frame. A plurality of light sources, such as light-emitting diodes, is mounted on the substrate to provide illumination to the display panel. A reflecting sheet is arranged over the substrate and includes apertures through which the respective light sources are exposed. The reflecting sheet reflects light traveling toward the rear frame back toward the display panel, thereby improving light-use efficiency.

The reflecting sheet further includes a side portion extending along an inner side surface of the rear frame. A plurality of light-absorbing dots is formed on at least part of this extended side portion. The dots are arranged so that their size increases with distance from a corner of the reflecting sheet in both a longitudinal direction and a transverse direction. As a result, the reflectance of the side portion is selectively reduced in regions where reflected light would otherwise tend to accumulate.

This graduated dot pattern compensates for differences in optical behavior near the corners and edges of the display device. By absorbing a controlled amount of light in selected regions, the pattern suppresses localized brightness and reduces luminance variations across the display panel. The display device can therefore provide more uniform illumination while retaining the reflective efficiency of the reflecting sheet in regions where additional light is needed.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” refers to a particular book that the speaker and listener already know about.

Although it is short and simple, “the” plays an essential role in communication. It adds clarity, creates emphasis, and helps connect ideas. Without it, many English sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. This small word demonstrates how even the simplest elements of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the structure of an LCD backlight assembly in formal patent language, including a rectangular reflector sheet with LED holes, an extension toward the frame sidewall, and graduated reflectance-reducing dots.
counterfactuals.output:
A backlight assembly for a liquid crystal display device comprises a frame having a bottom portion and a sidewall extending from the bottom portion; a substantially rectangular reflector sheet disposed within the frame; and a plurality of light-emitting diodes disposed in an array adjacent to the reflector sheet. The reflector sheet includes a plurality of through-holes corresponding respectively to the light-emitting diodes such that at least a light-emitting portion of each light-emitting diode is exposed through a respective through-hole. At least one peripheral edge of the reflector sheet includes an extension portion extending toward, and optionally along, an inner surface of the sidewall of the frame.

A plurality of reflectance-reducing dots is provided on the extension portion and/or a peripheral region of the reflector sheet adjacent thereto. The dots have a graduated distribution in which at least one of dot size, dot density, dot spacing, optical density, or surface coverage varies as a function of distance toward the sidewall. The graduated distribution progressively reduces the effective reflectance of the reflector sheet in the peripheral region, thereby suppressing localized luminance increases and improving luminance uniformity across an emission surface of the backlight assembly.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2
